analysis.title: U.S. First to Market
key_insights: DraftKings (DKNG, OW) reported a disappointing 3Q26. Adj. EBITDA loss of -$317m was nearly $250m below estimates (JPMe -$83m, Street -$68m). FY26 EBITDA guidance was cut by $575m to $225m (-70% vs. prior $800m). FY27 EBITDA guidance of $900m is about $200m below JPMe/Street at $1.1b.
Middleby (MIDD, OW) beat consensus across the P&L in 3Q and raised FY26 guidance. JPM sees mid-teens % EPS CAGR through 2028 within reach. Dec 27 PT raised to $165 from $145.

Cummins (CMI, N) missed 3Q sales consensus but beat on EPS and margins. Implied 4Q sales, margins and EPS guidance fell below consensus. JPM lowers 2027/28 EPS to $31.71/$37.67 and cuts PT to $465 from $600. Positioning going into the print skewed negative, and the print did not shift the bears.

Transportation & Logistics (Ossenbeck) took away views from the Association of Transportation Law Professionals Fall Forum in Washington, D.C. Attendance was down with the deadline for rail merger comments a few weeks away. The trip came days after the midterm elections.
Transportation & Logistics hosted an expert call with Prof. Jason Miller (Michigan State) on the state of freight and the 2027 outlook.
JPM hosts 26 companies at the Future of Freight event in Miami next week. The agenda covers autonomous freight handling (physical AI) plus private-company panels in brokerage, LTL and parcel.

The SMid View (Lecubarri): the June call to be cautious from June to October played out, with SMid indices down in every region except the UK, Japan and LatAm. The consumer remains a key worry, and JPM is assessing whether this is now a buying opportunity.

Daily Economic Briefing (Szentivanyi): the Bank of England delivered its first hike of the cycle with a more hawkish message signaling another one to two moves. The vote was 8-1, with Mann preferring 50bp. The case for hikes now extends beyond the energy shock, as the BoE raised growth forecasts, lowered unemployment-rate projections and acknowledged sticky services inflation. December is live, but JPM sticks to a February hike given this week's large drop in energy prices.

MKS (MKSI, OW, PT $380), Quantinuum (QNT, OW, PT $80) and Cloudflare (NET, OW, PT $375) all reported beat-and-raise or accelerating results. Cloudflare reported growth acceleration and stronger customer KPIs.
HMH was downgraded to Neutral from Overweight after a 3Q26 product slip and lack of visibility on the timing of floater realization.
Iron Mountain (IRM, OW) stock dropped on a tough day for the data center and AI thematic trade despite in-line results.
Hertz (HTZ, UW) posted a large miss on 3Q and 4Q guidance, with a slow turnaround and a thinning liquidity cushion.
Axon (AXON, OW) 3Q26 revenue missed on Dedrone delays, with a margin reset. PT cut to $610 from $755 and current-year EPS cut 11.9%.
Affirm (AFRM, OW) F1Q27 sticking points were explainable and October accelerated. Estimates were raised but PT was cut to $95 from $105.

Energy 3Q26 post-mortems: Tenaris (TS, OW) beat and raised with 2027E EBITDA up 11.6%. Devon (DVN, OW) portfolio review ended disappointingly but the 2027 guide is constructive. EOG (N) printed in line with an 8% dividend raise.
Healthcare Facilities: the final 2027 Medicare home health rate is up 370 bps y/y vs. the 2026 final rate.
JPM Focus List changes: Howmet (HWM), Quebecor (QBR/B CN) and Moody's (MCO) added 11/2. Boeing (BA), Xenon (XENE) and T-Mobile (TMUS) removed 11/2.
US October Employment Scorecard is listed, and the calendar shows the October payrolls consensus at 75,000 with unemployment at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.2%.
Upcoming US data: CPI Nov 10 per the calendar grid (listed under Nov 11 column order), PPI Nov 12, retail sales Nov 17, FOMC minutes Nov 19.
